-   **Rarity note:** Rare species in Florida, found in south-central prairie region.

## Natural history notes

A large, distinctive raptor characterized by its black cap and crest, pale neck, orange-red facial skin, heavy gray-blue bill, dark body, white wing patches, and long yellow legs. In Florida, it is found mainly in the south-central prairie region, especially open dry prairie, improved pasture, rangeland, cabbage palm areas, and other open habitats with scattered nesting trees. It feeds on carrion as well as live prey, including insects, reptiles, amphibians, birds, mammals, and eggs, often walking on the ground, patrolling roadsides for roadkill, or foraging in open fields. Its Florida population is listed as threatened, largely because of loss of dry prairie habitat.
